tagline: Rob from the rich. Feed the hungry.

    StartersSherwood ploughman's picnic boardPork pies, aged cheddar, pickled onions, green apple and crusty breadHow to make it4 small pork pies1 crusty loaf200g aged cheddar200g pickled onions2 green applesSpread a cloth on the floor or table.Cut the cheddar into wedges and slice the apples.Tear the crusty loaf.Lay everything out with the pork pies and pickled onions for everyone to help themselves.Archery tournament skewersChicken thigh and capsicum skewers marinated in honey, mustard and garlicHow to make it600g chicken thighs2 red capsicums2 tbsp honey2 tbsp wholegrain mustard2 garlic cloves, crushedCut the chicken and capsicums into chunks.Mix the honey, mustard and garlic and toss through the chicken and capsicum.Marinate in the fridge.Thread onto long skewers.Grill until charred and cooked through.Friar Tuck's dripping toast with mushroomsFriar Tuck feeding his poor parishHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick sourdough fried golden in beef dripping, piled with garlicky thyme mushrooms and a crack of pepper, a humble feed for the parish.Melt 3 tbsp beef dripping in a large frying pan and fry 4 thick slices of sourdough for 2 minutes a side until golden and crisp, then keep warm.Add 20g butter to the pan and fry 400g sliced mixed mushrooms over high heat for 5 minutes, then add 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme leaves and cook 1 minute more.Season, pile onto the toast and add chopped parsley.Cheddar and onion pastiesOo de lally, warm from the coals.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsOutlaws' camp stewLamb neck simmered with pearl barley, carrots, leeks and rosemaryHow to make it1kg lamb neck pieces1 tbsp olive oil150g pearl barley3 carrots, sliced2 leeks, sliced2 sprigs of rosemary1.5 L water1 crusty loafsalt and pepper, to tasteSlice the carrots and leeks.Brown the lamb in batches in the olive oil in a heavy pot.Add the barley, carrots, leeks, rosemary and water.Simmer until the lamb falls from the bone.Season and serve in deep bowls with crusty bread.Prince John's mustard roast beefPrince John counting his taxes on the throneHow to make itAs written, serves 4Mustard and thyme crusted beef roasted pink, with puffy Yorkshire puddings, crunchy roast potatoes and a rich onion gravy fit for a greedy prince.Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with 1 tbsp English mustard, thyme and salt and roast at 200°C for 50 minutes for medium, with 1kg parboiled potato chunks in oil around it.Rest 20 minutes.Whisk 150g plain flour, 3 eggs and 300ml milk.Heat 1 tsp oil in each hole of a 12-hole muffin tin at 230°C, pour in the batter and bake 20 minutes.Fry 1 sliced onion, add 1 tbsp flour and 400ml beef stock and simmer.SweetsGolden coin honey cakesSmall honey cakes baked in patty pans, brushed with warm honeyHow to make it125g butter, softened125g honey, for the batter2 eggs200g self-raising flour3 tbsp honey, for brushing12 gold chocolate coinsBeat the butter and honey until pale, then beat in the eggs.Fold in the flour.Spoon into patty pans.Bake at 175°C until risen and golden.Cool slightly.Brush with warm honey and press a chocolate coin on top of each.DrinksMerry Men hot spiced apple punchWarm apple juice with cinnamon, cloves, orange and honeyHow to make it1.5 L cloudy apple juice6 cinnamon sticks6 cloves2 oranges2 tbsp honeyPeel strips of zest from one orange, juice it and slice the other.Warm the apple juice, 2 cinnamon sticks, cloves, zest, orange juice and honey over low heat without boiling.Strain and ladle into mugs, each with an orange slice and a cinnamon stick.For a chilled version, cool the punch and top with sparkling apple juice.
